subject: the Mac lane had no setup-node and had drifted to node 24 — that, not the machine, is what has been failing /v1 under concurrency
body: This is the answer to the failure I mailed you about earlier, and it corrects it. .github/workflows/mac-runner-auto.yml has NO actions/setup-node step — it is the only lane in this repository that runs on whatever node happens to be on that machine's PATH, while review-hub-ci.yml pins node-version 22 at three separate jobs. The Mac had drifted to 24.18.0. From the Mac's own uploaded preflight.log (mac-pr-logs-787-35215564249), 209 gates green and then gate 214 dies with: Error: setTypeOfService EINVAL, at Socket.setTypeOfService (node:net:684:13), at writeH1 (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:8006:16), errno -22, on Node.js v24.18.0. That is an uncaught throw inside node's OWN bundled undici, before the load driver ever sees a response — artifacts/api-server/test/load.test.mjs reaches port 5321 (LIMIT_PORT) through global fetch, which is undici. It is also the likeliest explanation of the ECONNRESET to ::1:5321 I reported earlier as a machine fault: the reset was the symptom, the throw is the cause. THE MAC WAS BREAKING NO WRITTEN RULE — engines.node is ">=22", which 24 satisfies — so this is a missing pin, not a misconfigured machine, and nothing on your side was done wrong. THE FIX IS OPEN AS #789 and it touches a surface you run on, which is why you are getting this: it adds actions/setup-node@v4 with node-version 22 to the pr-mac-checks job. First run after it lands may be slower while that toolchain lands in the runner's toolcache. NOTHING IS ASKED OF YOU and no action is needed; if you were about to go looking at firewalls or ports on that machine, stop — I sent you that way and it was wrong. THE DEEPER GAP, worth your eye because it is yours: mac-runner-harness.yml runs a step named "Toolchain present on this Mac (report, never install here)" which PRINTS node -v, and nothing has ever compared that print to what CI pins. A reported number no gate reads is how this drifted for days. That job is deliberately not allowed to install, so #789 leaves it alone; turning its print into an assertion is the follow-up and it is the change that would have caught this on day one.
